panel.title: Survey drawing of a round Ifá tray (25 cm) with a rim of twelve repeated fish-head units
panel.object_type: pen-and-ink survey drawing of a round opon Ifá
panel.summary: A drawing captioned 'Ifabrett, 25 cm diameter, Yoruba 3' of a small round tray. A face at the head and a ribbed block at the foot sit on one axis; between them the rim carries about twelve identical units — rounded forms with a hatched 'fin' and an open V, six on each side.

register_readings.reading: The head: two lozenge eyes and a nose between ribbed blocks (plus blank card).
Rim (undetected): six identical units down each side, facing alternately.
Foot (undetected): a ribbed block opposite the face.

panel.composition: A strict ring: one face, one block, and a regular sequence of identical units in between.
panel.narrative: The simplest, most regular tray in the collection. The repeated unit looks like a fish head or a bird; if it is a fish head it recalls the agbérí ẹja ('fish head') pattern that Aronson tied to Olókun in Ijebu cloth — a motif moving between cloth and wood. A tray built from twelve identical units between two fixed points is also the clearest case here of carved pattern that could be counted.
panel.hypotheses: Neutral for 'chronicle'. Strongest tray candidate for 'pattern as number': twelve units (or fourteen compartments with face and block) — to compare against Ifá counts, which it does not obviously match (16).
